title: Meeting the Handler
logline: The Collective crosses a line it swore it wouldn't. Nadia brings everyone to the Network, and the Network is perfectly, unnervingly polite about it. The visual arc runs from street to doorstep to a bare room to one small card.
questions: The Handler has no reference and no canon look. Proposal: deliberately forgettable. Fifties, neat plain suit or a good cardigan, reading glasses, the most ordinary person in the room. The menace is in the tidiness, not in the face. Gender, age and look are your call. Whatever we pick becomes the reference for every later Network scene.

Des 'with his coat buttoned to the top': his reference has an open navy overshirt. Proposal: a dark wool overcoat, buttoned to the collar, over the same outfit. It's the visible sign of his discomfort. Is that OK as a costume change?
Player face: the player picks their own sprite, so these shots keep 'you' faceless (POV or out of frame). Is that the rule for all event art, or should the player appear?

Time of day isn't in the text. Proposal: weekday early evening, overcast and damp, street lamps just on. That matches the Act 1 Collective art's dusk mood. Alternative: flat grey midday, which reads more 'business meeting'.
Budget: 4 core shots across 9 cards, plus 2 optional cuts (S2b, S3b). Approve an optional shot to add it, or cut it to keep the board lean.

cards.text: Nadia doesn't ask if you're free. She texts an address in Clerkenwell and a time, and then she's waiting on the corner when you get there.
cards.why: New location. Card 1 can't start blank. Nadia waiting tells you who called this meeting.

cards.speaker: Nadia
cards.text: "I know we said not yet. That was before something we couldn't explain took a vein we'd done everything right by. I'm done waiting for an explanation to turn up on its own."
cards.why: Same moment, her line. S1 is framed close enough that her resolve reads on her face.

cards.text: Des is already there, on the step, with his coat buttoned to the top. He came. Nobody asked him to and nobody asked him not to.
cards.why: Reveal. Des is held out of S1 so he lands here. The buttoned coat is the whole beat.

cards.speaker: Des
cards.text: "For the record, I think this is a mistake. I'd like that written down somewhere."
cards.why: His objection plays over his own shot.

cards.text: Nadia holds the door. He looks at it for a moment, then goes in first. It is the least comfortable you have ever seen him.
cards.why: S2's closed door, with Nadia's hand reaching for it, carries this. Optional S2b would cut here.

cards.text: The office is small and very tidy. The handler stands when you come in, shakes everyone's hand, and asks after Hakim by name.
cards.why: New location, new character. First uncluttered room in the Collective's story.

cards.speaker: Handler
cards.text: "Two things, and I'll be brief. Name a vein you think is weak and I'll tell you whether it is. Name what you want in the ground and I'll find you one."
cards.why: The pitch plays over the room. Optional S3b would cut to the Handler's face here.

cards.speaker: Handler
cards.text: "Everything I tell you will be true. You'll pay for it either way. That includes the answers you don't like."
cards.why: Same conversation. A cut here would only dilute S4.

cards.text: The handler writes a number on the back of a card and slides it across. Nobody is hurried out. There is no need.
cards.why: Payoff insert. The deal is one small object. Cheap to make and the most memorable frame.

shots.title: Nadia on the Clerkenwell corner
shots.job: Place and pressure: Nadia summoned you, and she's already decided.
shots.instant: Nadia stands on the corner, phone lowered in one hand, turned toward camera as 'you' arrive. Her expression is set, not warm.
shots.framing: Medium-wide, eye level, from across the narrow street (player POV approaching). Nadia framed from about the knees up, so her face reads on a phone.
shots.composition: Nadia centre-left, midground. Behind her, a Georgian brick terrace corner: black railings, sash windows, one plain dark front door with a small brass plate (no letters) screen-right. Foreground: kerb edge and wet road.
shots.light: Early evening, overcast, damp. Street lamp key from screen-left, warm, on Nadia. Cool grey-blue sky; lit windows are the only other warm notes.
shots.crop: Nadia's face and hands in the central band. Sky and road at the top and bottom edges.
shots.unseen: Des. The step and the door's surroundings stay empty or out of frame. He's revealed on card 3.

shots.title: Des on the step, coat buttoned
shots.job: Des came anyway, and hates it. His posture makes the objection before he speaks.
shots.instant: Des stands on the doorstep, coat buttoned to the collar, hands in pockets, looking at the closed door rather than at anyone. Nadia's hand enters frame screen-left, reaching for the door.
shots.framing: Medium shot, slight low angle from the pavement (a step's height below him). It gives the doorway weight and makes the door the destination.
shots.composition: The door is centre, dark gloss paint, brass plate and intercom panel with no legible text. Des is screen-right on the step, which is on the same side as the door in S1 (180° rule). Nadia appears only as a cardigan sleeve and hand, screen-left foreground.
shots.light: Same as S1: lamp key from screen-left, warm on brick, cool shadows. A wet sheen on the stone step.
shots.crop: Des's face, the buttoned collar, and the door handle in the centre band.
shots.unseen: The inside of the building. The door stays closed.

shots.title: Optional: reverse angle, Des on the threshold
shots.job: Turn the hesitation into a held breath. Shot from inside, the open door frames Des against the street, the last moment before he crosses.
shots.instant: From inside the dim hallway looking out: the door is open, Nadia holds it (half in frame), and Des stands on the threshold looking in at us. He hasn't stepped yet.
shots.framing: Medium shot, eye level, from deep in the hallway. The doorway is a bright rectangle in a dark frame.
shots.composition: Dark hallway walls frame the doorway (natural letterbox). Des is centred in the doorway, Nadia screen-left holding the door, and the street lamp glows behind them. Hallway floor in the foreground: plain, clean, no clutter.
shots.light: Backlit: the street is brighter than the hallway, so Des is partly silhouetted with lamp rim light. A cooler interior tone.
shots.crop: Des's face (rim-lit, readable) in the centre. The dark edges can crop freely.

shots.title: The tidy office, the Handler standing
shots.job: Introduce the Handler and the Network's register: courteous, ordered, nothing out of place. Polite enough to be frightening.
shots.instant: The Handler has just stood up behind a bare desk and is half-turned toward Nadia with a hand extended. Des stands stiffly just inside the door.
shots.framing: Wide-medium, eye level, player POV from the doorway. It takes in the whole small room.
shots.composition: The desk is centre and nearly empty: a closed notepad, one pen, squared exactly. The Handler is behind it, centre-right. Nadia is screen-left, mid-step toward the desk. Des is screen-right edge by the wall, coat still buttoned. Background: a plain wall, one frameless print, a window with half-closed blinds, a coat stand.
shots.light: Interior. Cool daylight through the blinds, plus one warm desk lamp. Clean, even, uncluttered. A visual contrast with every Collective room so far.
shots.crop: The Handler's face and hand, and the desk top, in the centre band.
shots.unseen: The business card, the number, any Network iconography.
shots.canon: The Handler's look. See open questions.

shots.title: Optional: the Handler, across the desk
shots.job: Put a face on 'everything I tell you will be true'. A calm, direct address to the player.
shots.instant: The Handler is seated, forearms resting on the desk, hands loosely folded, looking straight into the lens with a small, patient expression.
shots.framing: Medium close-up, eye level, player POV across the desk.
shots.composition: The Handler is centred. The desk edge runs across the lower frame. The blinds are soft behind them.
shots.light: Same as S3. The warm desk lamp lights one side of the face.
shots.crop: The face in the upper-centre third. The hands may crop on a small phone.

shots.title: Insert: the card slid across the desk
shots.job: The deal, reduced to one small object. A quiet, final image.
shots.instant: The Handler's fingertips push a plain white business card across the bare desk toward camera. Handwritten digits are on the back, shown as pen strokes with no legible numbers.
shots.framing: Insert / close-up, high angle looking down at the desk surface from the player's seat.
shots.composition: The card is centre. The Handler's hand and cuff enter from the top of frame. The rest is empty desk wood, the squared notepad and the pen, slightly out of focus.
shots.light: Warm desk-lamp pool on the card, cool falloff to the edges.
shots.crop: The card and fingertips dead centre.
continuity: S3 approved draft (same desk and props)
